blogPosts.title: How Much Does Custom Joinery Cost in Southbank? 2026 Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: A breakdown of joinery costs in Southbank for built-in wardrobes, cabinets, and shelving. What to expect on price.
body: Custom joinery in Southbank can vary a lot based on the size, timber type, and finish. For a typical built-in wardrobe in a one-bedroom apartment, you're looking at around $1,500 to $3,000 for materials and labour, with plywood being the most common choice. Here's the full rundown on what affects the cost.

The type of timber is the biggest factor. Australian hardwoods like blackbutt or spotted gum are more expensive than plantation pine or MDF, but they last decades. In Southbank, many apartments use MDF with a veneer finish to keep costs down and match the existing cabinetry.

Labour is the next big cost. A skilled carpenter will charge between $60 and $90 per hour for joinery work, and most jobs take between one and three days. A full kitchen fit-out can take a week or more, so the labour adds up fast. We always quote the total job, not an hourly rate, so you know exactly where you stand.

Additional costs like hardware, handles, and soft-close mechanisms can add $200 to $500 to a joinery project. We use high-quality Blum and Hettich hardware for smooth operation and long life. It's worth spending the extra on good hinges and drawer slides.

If you live in a period-style Southbank apartment, you may need heritage-compliant materials or custom sizes. This can increase the cost by 10 to 20 percent due to extra measuring and adjustments. We work with the existing layout to keep things clean and avoid unnecessary expense.

A good rule of thumb is to budget $2,500 to $5,000 for a decent-sized custom joinery project in Southbank, including installation and finishing. We've seen everything from small shelf units at $800 to full wall-to-wall systems at $8,000. Get in touch for a tailored quote.

Timber choice also affects the look. Australian blackwood has a warm tone that suits Southbank's older homes, while American oak is lighter and more modern. We can source both. If you're after something sustainable, we use FSC-certified timber on request.

Remember to factor in delivery and installation. We include delivery within 10km of our Southbank workshop for free. For bigger jobs, we can drop materials directly to your site and assemble on the day. That saves you hassle and keeps the job moving.

blogPosts.title: Best Timber for Southbank Kitchen Cabinets: A Local Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Choosing the right timber for your Southbank kitchen. Plywood, MDF, and solid options compared for cost and durability.
body: When it comes to kitchen cabinets in Southbank, the main timber options are plywood, MDF, and solid hardwood. Each has its pros and cons depending on your budget and style. Here's what you need to know before choosing.

Plywood is the go-to for most custom cabinets. It's strong, stable, and holds screws well. We use 18mm plywood for carcasses and 6mm for backs. The cost is around $80 to $120 per sheet, and it's available in birch, hoop pine, and other species. In Southbank, ply is popular for its durability and clean look.

MDF is cheaper at $40 to $60 per sheet but not as strong. It's fine for painted cabinets where you won't see the grain, but it can swell if it gets wet. For Southbank kitchens, we recommend avoiding MDF for cabinets near the sink unless it's moisture-resistant grade.

Solid hardwood like blackbutt or spotted gum is the premium option. It's beautiful, durable, and will last a lifetime. The cost is $150 to $250 per square metre for the timber alone, plus extra for joinery and finishing. It's a big investment but worth it if you want a custom look.

For most Southbank kitchens, we use a mix: plywood for the carcass and hardwood veneer or solid wood for the doors and drawer fronts. This gives you the look of hardwood without the full cost. It also reduces weight on the hinges.

Finishes matter too. Lacquer or oil-based finishes protect the timber and make it easier to clean. We use water-based finishes for low odour. In Southbank's apartment kitchens, that's a big plus because the space is often enclosed and you don't want fumes.

If you're on a tight budget, we can do a laminate or polyurethane finish that looks like timber but is cheaper. The cost drops to around $80 per square metre for the doors. It's a good option for rental properties or first homes.

Always check the timber's moisture content. In Melbourne's climate, timber should be around 10 to 12 percent moisture. We test every piece before we cut to avoid warping. That's a step many cheap joiners skip, but we don't.

Finally, think about the colour. Southbank's light-filled apartments suit lighter timbers like birch or ash. Darker timbers like walnut or mahogany work well in period homes. We can show you samples in our workshop to pick the right match.

blogPosts.title: How to Maintain Your Timber Floor in Southbank Apartment
blogPosts.excerpt: Timber floor maintenance tips for Southbank residents. Keep your floors looking new for years with simple care.
body: Timber floors in Southbank apartments need regular care to stay looking good. The biggest enemy is moisture and grit. If you have hardwood floors, here's a simple maintenance plan to keep them in top shape.

Sweep or vacuum at least once a week. Grit and sand scratch the surface over time. Use a soft-bristled broom or a vacuum with a floor head. Avoid wet mops if possible, because standing water can seep into the gaps and cause swelling.

In Melbourne's climate, timber floors expand and contract with humidity. In summer, you might see small gaps between boards. In winter, they close up. That's normal and no cause for concern. But if you see large gaps or cupping, it could mean a moisture issue.

Use a pH-neutral timber floor cleaner designed for your floor's finish. We recommend Bona or similar brands. Avoid ammonia or vinegar because they can strip the lacquer. For high-traffic areas, a weekly clean with a spray mop is enough.

Re-coating your floor every 3 to 5 years keeps the finish fresh. In Southbank, many apartments have a satin or matte finish that shows less wear. You can do a light coat yourself or hire a pro. The cost is around $30 to $50 per square metre for a full re-sand and coat.

If you have pets, use scratch guards on their claws. A simple nail trim and a rug in high-traffic areas can extend the floor's life by years. We see a lot of Southbank apartments with pet-friendly floors, and the main trick is keeping claws short.

Watch out for sun bleaching. Southbank's west-facing windows can fade timber over time. Rotate furniture and use blinds during peak sun hours. A UV-protective finish can help. Ask us about the right product for your floor.

Stains from red wine or coffee are best treated immediately with a damp cloth. If they dry, you may need a light sand. We always recommend keeping a spare tin of the same finish in case you need a touch-up. Store it in the cupboard under the sink.

Finally, consider a mat at the entrance to catch grit before it hits the floor. A simple walk-off mat can cut down on scratches and wear. That's the cheapest and most effective step for any Southbank apartment.

blogPosts.title: Why Choose a Local Carpenter for Your Southbank Renovation?
blogPosts.excerpt: Benefits of hiring a local carpenter in Southbank for your renovation. Faster, cheaper, and better quality work.
body: Hiring a local carpenter for your Southbank renovation means you get someone who knows the area, the building types, and the suppliers. It's not just about convenience, it's about getting the job done right first time.

A local carpenter can visit your site quickly to measure up and give a quote in person. No driving across town, no guessing. That saves time and money. For a renovation in Southbank, being local cuts down on travel time and the risk of delays.

Local carpenters know the council rules for Southbank and the surrounding suburbs. We know what permits are needed for structural work and what can be done without approval. That saves you the headache of council fines or stop-work orders later.

We also know the local timber suppliers. We can source materials from the same yards you'd use, but at trade prices. That means better timber and lower cost than a builder from out of town. We've been using the same suppliers for years.

A local carpenter is accountable. If something goes wrong, we're in the phone book and right around the corner. We can't afford bad work because we live here and work here. Our reputation in Southbank is everything.

In a renovation, a local carpenter can coordinate with other trades like plumbers and electricians because they know the same crews. That keeps the project running smoothly. You don't want a plumber from Brighton who doesn't know Southbank's pipe layout.

Price-wise, a local carpenter is often cheaper than a big company because we don't have the overheads. We work from a van and a small workshop, not a showroom. Our quotes are competitive and based on real experience, not guesswork.

Most Southbank renovations are in apartment blocks or heritage buildings. A local carpenter knows how to work around those constraints, from noise hours to building access. That's something a general builder might not get.

If you're thinking of a renovation in Southbank, call a local carpenter first. You'll get better advice, a fairer price, and a job that's done right. We're happy to come and look at your project and talk options.
